name: AI audits for small businesses
one_liner: Interview a small business owner on a 45-minute video call, use Claude to turn the transcript into an AI-adoption report, then upsell implementation work.
customer: Small business owners who know they should use AI but don't know where to start
offer: Fixed-fee AI audit: a recorded interview (on a call or through a voice agent), a written report recommending specific AI tools for their pain points, and a follow-up call
how_it_makes_money: About $1,000 per audit, followed by $3,000–$5,000 implementation upsells
startup_cost: low - 'basically no cost' (Zoom, Claude, optional voice agent)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; the host says about 7 days of study is enough to sell it
evidence: 'selling AI audits to small business owners for $1,000 with basically no cost' (03DjE7j0Suw)
A successful friend offered to pay $1,000 for a day of AI advice (03DjE7j0Suw)
'talking to probably 50 to 100 different business owners... 99 out of a 100 people need the service' (03DjE7j0Suw)
'That's a three to $5,000 upsell all day' (03DjE7j0Suw)
risks: Calls are needed for both selling and delivery
Many people are entering the 'AI consultant' space
Value depends on the upsell actually being delivered
Trust is hard to build without a track record

name: Build-first websites for local businesses on a monthly subscription
one_liner: Use AI to build a website for a local business before contacting them, show it to the owner, and charge a monthly fee to keep it live.
customer: Local SMBs with no website or a poor one (trades, services)
offer: A ready-made website plus hosting and maintenance, with upsells such as CRM, reviews and automations
how_it_makes_money: Recurring $50–$100/month per site (example price $75/month), with near-zero marginal cost per client
startup_cost: low - GoHighLevel at about $50/month after a 30-day free trial; agent-built sites cost 'a handful of cents' each in tokens
time_to_first_revenue: days to weeks (outreach by text or cold message after the site is built)
evidence: 'pay me 75 bucks a month... monthly cost to maintain it? Almost zero' (_aGMxMmJJj4)
'dozens and hundreds of business owners... 50 to 100 bucks a month... making tens of thousands a month' (_aGMxMmJJj4)
An AI agent found 350 Utah businesses, built 350 websites, and produced 'a little over 8K a month in MRR' (1PwTrINNzOA)
Each site cost 'a handful of cents' in tokens (1PwTrINNzOA)
risks: Cold texting is restricted under UK/EU rules (PECR/GDPR); outreach should use email or LinkedIn with care
Commoditised offer with high churn
GoHighLevel lock-in
Many other people copy this playbook

name: Multilingual voice-cloned voicemails for estate agents
one_liner: Clone an agent's voice and produce a library of personalised voicemails in their clients' native languages.
customer: Estate agents and realtors whose buyer base includes many non-native speakers
offer: Done-for-you voice clone plus pre-recorded multilingual voicemail and alert library (new listing, price drop, showing confirmation, etc.)
startup_cost: low - voice-cloning subscription plus an LLM
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; build described as 'very easy' and quick
evidence: '40% of home buyers speak a language other than English at home... over 50%' in some US markets (trdHxY1UMF0)
'charge $200 to $500 a month' (trdHxY1UMF0)
Needs only a 30–60 second audio clip to clone a voice (trdHxY1UMF0)
No real paying customer is shown, so evidence is weak to medium
risks: Demand evidence is US-centric; UK and Portuguese markets need validation
Consent and deepfake perception issues
Agents can do this themselves once tools become simpler
Ringless voicemail rules differ in the UK and EU

name: Instant quote and job-profit tools for trades
one_liner: Build simple no-code apps (an instant quote generator and a job profit tracker) for home service businesses and charge setup plus a monthly fee.
customer: Home service and trades owners (garage door repair and similar)
offer: Branded instant-quote web tool to capture leads quickly, plus a job profit tracker
how_it_makes_money: Upfront setup fee plus a monthly subscription (amounts not stated)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; the host claims to find a customer live on camera
evidence: '78% of customers will hire the first company that gives them a quote' (DKqQe0MqDTs)
'pay you upfront and every single month to use this tool' (DKqQe0MqDTs)
No revenue figures are given, so evidence is weak
risks: Prices are unstated
Tradespeople are hard to reach and sell to
Competes with existing field-service SaaS (Jobber, Tradify)

name: Niche Claude skills as digital products
one_liner: Package your own domain know-how into Claude Code skills and sell them as downloadable digital products.
customer: Professionals and marketers who use Claude Code or Claude
offer: A 'skill stack' (bundled Claude skills) for a specific workflow
how_it_makes_money: One-off digital product sales through Stripe
time_to_first_revenue: 30–45 days to over $3,000 in the case shown
evidence: 'launched this about 30 to 45 days ago. It's made over $3,000 just passively' (quYKZushRPo)
The seller already had an audience as the owner of a six-figure solo marketing agency (quYKZushRPo)

Easy to copy
Small, early market
Platform changes could undercut it

name: Vibe-coded niche AI consumer apps
one_liner: Build narrow AI apps with no-code or vibe-coding tools for a specific hobby niche and grow them with short-form content.
customer: Consumers in a specific niche (e.g. wrestlers or fighters wanting AI training)
time_to_first_revenue: 1 week ($8K in the first week); later apps reached $10K in 45 days
evidence: '225,000 in like nine months of building five coding apps without any coding experience' (oaXnY1YExjE)
'two latest apps were able to scale both to 10K in 45 days' (oaXnY1YExjE)
A peer's app was sold to MyFitnessPal (oaXnY1YExjE)
risks: Hit-driven, with high variance
Growth depends on paid or viral distribution
App store fees and churn

name: AI-produced faceless YouTube channels
one_liner: Run a faceless niche YouTube channel produced with AI tools, earning from ads and affiliates, then sell the channel.
customer: YouTube (AdSense), affiliate partners, and buyers of channels
how_it_makes_money: AdSense at $15–$30 RPM for finance or $3–$8 for storytelling, plus affiliate commissions; a channel earning $3K/month can sell for about $100K
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (needs the YPP threshold; usually months)
evidence: 'Faceless channels are making people 5, 10, even 30 grand a month' is a general claim with no specific case, so evidence is weak (utOHNPN0IlQ)
'channel doing three grand a month... will sell for about 100,000' (utOHNPN0IlQ)
risks: YouTube demonetises 'inauthentic' or mass-produced AI content
Slow to reach monetisation
Saturated market

name: Themed bingo nights with pub partners (plant bingo)
one_liner: Run ticketed themed bingo nights in bars on their quiet nights, with prizes tied to the theme (such as plants).
customer: Consumers buying event tickets; venues gain off-night footfall
how_it_makes_money: Ticket sales; about $21K–$25K per month and close to $1,000/hour profit
time_to_first_revenue: first event sold out in 4–5 days; $30K profit in the first two months

Partners with 20–30K followers shared the content (r8-FG4NJ39s)

Fad risk
